landmarks.name: Empire State Building
landmarks.fact: Finished in 1931 in just 410 days, it was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.

landmarks.name: Times Square
landmarks.fact: Named for The New York Times, which moved here in 1904. The New Year's Eve ball first dropped in 1907.

landmarks.name: Rockefeller Center
landmarks.fact: Built during the Great Depression, it employed some 40,000 people. The famous tree tradition began in 1931.

landmarks.name: Chrysler Building
landmarks.fact: Its stainless-steel spire was assembled secretly inside the building and hoisted into place in 90 minutes.

landmarks.name: United Nations Headquarters
landmarks.fact: The land along the East River is international territory, donated by John D. Rockefeller Jr. in 1946.

landmarks.name: Flatiron Building
landmarks.fact: Its triangular shape follows the wedge where Broadway crosses Fifth Avenue. At its narrowest it's about 2 m wide.

landmarks.name: Madison Square Garden
landmarks.fact: The current arena is the fourth MSG. It sits on top of Penn Station, the busiest rail hub in North America.

landmarks.name: Bryant Park
landmarks.fact: Once a reservoir site and a potter's field, it now hosts a winter skating rink and outdoor movie nights.

landmarks.name: Bethesda Terrace
landmarks.fact: Its fountain angel, sculpted by Emma Stebbins in 1873, was the first major public art commission in NYC given to a woman.

landmarks.name: Columbus Circle
landmarks.fact: All official distances to and from New York City are measured from this circle.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Center
landmarks.fact: It replaced the San Juan Hill neighborhood, the setting that inspired West Side Story.

landmarks.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
landmarks.fact: The Met holds over two million objects, including a complete Egyptian temple, the Temple of Dendur.

landmarks.name: Guggenheim Museum
landmarks.fact: Frank Lloyd Wright's spiral took 16 years from commission to opening in 1959, months after he died.

landmarks.name: American Museum of Natural History
landmarks.fact: Its 94-foot blue whale model hangs in the Hall of Ocean Life and gets a vacuum-cleaning once a year.

landmarks.name: Apollo Theater
landmarks.fact: Amateur Night launched Ella Fitzgerald, James Brown and Jimi Hendrix. Performers still rub the 'Tree of Hope' stump for luck.

landmarks.name: Columbia University
landmarks.fact: Founded in 1754 as King's College, it is the oldest college in New York State.

landmarks.name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
landmarks.fact: Construction began in 1892 and it is still unfinished. It is nicknamed 'St. John the Unfinished'.

landmarks.name: Washington Square Park
landmarks.fact: The marble arch was built in 1892 to mark the centennial of George Washington's inauguration.

landmarks.name: Union Square
landmarks.fact: The first American Labor Day parade marched here in 1882. The Greenmarket runs four days a week.

landmarks.name: Whitney Museum & High Line
landmarks.fact: The High Line is a 2.3 km park built on a freight rail viaduct that closed in 1980.

landmarks.name: Chelsea Market
landmarks.fact: The building was the Nabisco factory where the Oreo cookie was invented in 1912.

landmarks.name: The Vessel at Hudson Yards
landmarks.fact: Hudson Yards is built on a platform over an active rail yard that still stores Long Island Rail Road trains.

landmarks.name: World Trade Center & 9/11 Memorial
landmarks.fact: One World Trade Center is 1,776 feet tall, a nod to the year of the Declaration of Independence.

landmarks.name: New York Stock Exchange
landmarks.fact: The exchange traces its origin to the 1792 Buttonwood Agreement, signed by 24 brokers under a buttonwood tree.

landmarks.name: Charging Bull
landmarks.fact: Arturo Di Modica installed the 3-ton bronze bull without permission in 1989. The city kept it.

landmarks.name: The Battery
landmarks.fact: Castle Clinton here was America's first immigration station, processing 8 million people before Ellis Island opened.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Bridge Entrance
landmarks.fact: When it opened in 1883, P.T. Barnum led 21 elephants across to prove the bridge was sturdy.

landmarks.name: South Street Seaport
landmarks.fact: This was the city's main port in the 1800s; its cobblestone streets date to that era.

landmarks.name: Chinatown (Mott Street)
landmarks.fact: Mott Street was the heart of Manhattan's Chinatown from the 1870s, and Doyers Street was once called the Bloody Angle.

landmarks.name: Little Italy (Mulberry Street)
landmarks.fact: The Feast of San Gennaro has filled Mulberry Street every September since 1926.

landmarks.name: Tenement Museum
landmarks.fact: 97 Orchard Street housed an estimated 7,000 people from 20 nations between 1863 and 1935.

landmarks.name: Stonewall Inn
landmarks.fact: The 1969 uprising here sparked the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement. It became a national monument in 2016.

landmarks.name: St. Patrick's Cathedral
landmarks.fact: Its spires were the tallest point in the city when completed in 1888.

landmarks.name: Carnegie Hall
landmarks.fact: Tchaikovsky conducted on opening night in 1891.

landmarks.name: Museum of Modern Art
landmarks.fact: MoMA is home to Van Gogh's The Starry Night and Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans.

landmarks.name: Intrepid Museum
landmarks.fact: The aircraft carrier Intrepid survived five kamikaze attacks in WWII and later recovered NASA astronauts.

landmarks.name: Tompkins Square Park
landmarks.fact: Its American elm, the Hare Krishna Tree, is where the movement's first US chant was held in 1966.

landmarks.name: The Cloisters
landmarks.fact: Parts of five medieval French monasteries were shipped over and rebuilt here; it opened in 1938.

landmarks.name: General Grant National Memorial
landmarks.fact: It is the largest mausoleum in North America. The answer to 'Who's buried in Grant's Tomb?' is Grant and his wife Julia.

landmarks.name: Strawberry Fields
landmarks.fact: The 'Imagine' mosaic was a gift from the city of Naples, Italy.

landmarks.name: Central Park Zoo
landmarks.fact: The Delacorte Clock above the zoo plays nursery rhymes as bronze animals circle every half hour.

landmarks.name: Gracie Mansion
landmarks.fact: Built in 1799 as a merchant's country house, it has been the mayor's residence since 1942.

landmarks.name: Roosevelt Island Tramway
landmarks.fact: Opened in 1976 as a temporary link, it was the first commuter aerial tramway in North America.

landmarks.name: Hamilton Grange
landmarks.fact: Alexander Hamilton's only home. The house has been moved twice, most recently in 2008, rolled on steel beams.

landmarks.name: Chelsea Piers
landmarks.fact: The Titanic was headed for Pier 59 here. The survivors were brought in on the Carpathia instead.

targets.name: Grand Central Terminal
targets.clue: Find the station where the ceiling shows the stars.
facts: The zodiac on its ceiling is painted backwards, as if seen from outside the heavens.
Its four-faced clock above the information booth is said to be worth millions.

targets.name: New York Public Library
targets.clue: Find the place where the city keeps its oldest books.
facts: Two stone lions named Patience and Fortitude guard its front steps.
It sits right beside a park that was once a reservoir.

targets.name: The Morgan Library & Museum
targets.clue: Find a banker's private treasure room of medieval manuscripts.
facts: It was built for J.P. Morgan, the most powerful banker of the Gilded Age.
It owns three Gutenberg Bibles.

targets.name: Federal Hall
targets.clue: Find where the first president swore his oath.
facts: A bronze statue of George Washington stands on its steps.
It faces the most famous stock exchange in the world.

targets.name: Fraunces Tavern
targets.clue: Find the tavern where a general said farewell to his officers.
facts: George Washington bid his officers goodbye here in 1783.
It's a red-brick colonial building on one of the oldest streets in the city.

targets.name: Katz's Delicatessen
targets.clue: Find the deli where the pastrami is still carved by hand.
facts: A famous movie scene about 'what she's having' was filmed at one of its tables.
During WWII it urged: 'Send a salami to your boy in the army.'

targets.name: Hotel Chelsea
targets.clue: Find the hotel where artists once paid rent in paintings.
facts: Mark Twain, Bob Dylan and Patti Smith all stayed here.
It is a red-brick building with cast-iron balconies on West 23rd Street.

targets.name: Strand Bookstore
targets.clue: Find the shop that boasts eighteen miles of books.
facts: It sits on the last surviving block of what was once 'Book Row'.
It is a short walk from a square famous for its farmers market.

targets.name: The Dakota
targets.clue: Find the apartment house named because it seemed as far away as the frontier.
facts: John Lennon lived here, across the street from the park memorial that bears his song's name.
It was the setting of the film Rosemary's Baby.

targets.name: Belvedere Castle
targets.clue: Find a castle built only to be looked at.
facts: It is a Victorian folly on Vista Rock, the second-highest point in the park.
It hosts the weather station that reports Central Park's official temperature.

targets.name: The Frick Collection
targets.clue: Find a steel baron's mansion filled with Old Masters.
facts: Henry Clay Frick built the mansion so his collection could become a museum after his death.
It faces Central Park across Fifth Avenue.

targets.name: St. Paul's Chapel
targets.clue: Find the oldest church still standing in Manhattan.
facts: It was built in 1766 and George Washington prayed here after his inauguration.
It survived 9/11 untouched and became a relief station for recovery workers.

targets.name: Trinity Church
targets.clue: Find the churchyard where a ten-dollar founder rests.
facts: Alexander Hamilton is buried in its churchyard.
It stands at the head of Wall Street.

targets.name: Tiffany & Co. Fifth Avenue
targets.clue: Find the window where a movie heroine ate her breakfast.
facts: Audrey Hepburn ate a pastry outside its windows in a 1961 film.
It is known for its robin's-egg blue boxes.

targets.name: The Plaza Hotel
targets.clue: Find the hotel where a mischievous six-year-old lives on the top floor.
facts: The children's book character Eloise lives here.
It faces Grand Army Plaza at the southeast corner of the city's biggest park.

targets.name: Macy's Herald Square
targets.clue: Find the store behind the most famous Thanksgiving parade.
facts: It once called itself the world's largest store, filling a full city block.
Some of its wooden escalators, from the 1900s, still run.

targets.name: Sylvia's Restaurant
targets.clue: Find the kitchen of the Queen of Soul Food.
facts: Sylvia Woods opened it in 1962 with just a counter and a few booths.
It is on Malcolm X Boulevard (Lenox Avenue).

targets.name: Little Red Lighthouse
targets.clue: Find the little lighthouse that sits beneath a great gray bridge.
facts: A 1942 children's book saved it from demolition.
It stands under the George Washington Bridge on the Hudson.
